claim: YouTube requires monetized (YPP) creators to clear five sequential revenue thresholds before money moves: tax info threshold (USD 0, immediate), verification threshold (USD 10), payment method selection threshold (USD 10), payment threshold (USD 100), and cancelation threshold (USD 10).
stance_target: structure of the payout gate between 'monetized' and 'paid'
scope_conditions: global YPP creators, USD reporting currency; other currencies have separately listed values
quoted_support: The revenue thresholds you need to meet before getting paid are: Tax info threshold, Verification threshold, Payment method selection threshold, Payment threshold, Cancelation threshold.

claim: The USD payment threshold -- the point at which a creator actually receives money -- is $100; earnings below this accrue but are not disbursed.
stance_target: quantifying time-to-first-income delay caused by the payout floor
quoted_support: When your earnings reach the payment threshold, then you'll get paid as long as there are no holds on your account.

claim: If a creator does not submit tax info, Google may withhold up to 24% of that creator's total worldwide YouTube earnings -- a mandatory deduction applied regardless of the creator's home country.
stance_target: hidden reduction of gross creator income independent of ad revenue share
scope_conditions: global YPP creators who have not submitted tax info to Google
quoted_support: If you don't share your tax info with us, Google may be required to deduct up to 24% of your total earnings worldwide.

claim: The payment threshold is currency-localized rather than uniformly proportional: Indonesian rupiah is set at Rp1,300,000 (approximately USD 80) and Singapore dollar at S$150 (approximately USD 112), both diverging from the flat USD 100 anchor.
stance_target: Southeast Asia-specific payout threshold data (only two SEA currencies listed)
scope_conditions: Indonesia and Singapore only among Southeast Asian currencies; Thailand, Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia have no locally listed threshold on this page and by omission fall under the USD 100 (or nearest-equivalent) floor
quoted_support: Indonesian rupiah (IDR) ... Rp130000 [verification/method] | Rp1300000 [payment threshold] | Rp130000 [cancelation]; Singapore Dollar (SGD) ... S$15 | S$150 | S$15

claim: Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, and Malaysia have no locally-denominated payment threshold listed on YouTube's official threshold table, an explicit gap in platform disclosure for major Southeast Asian creator markets.
stance_target: flag for SEA generalizability -- absence of disclosed local thresholds for 4 of 6 major SEA countries
scope_conditions: scope limited to the 29-currency table on this specific page as of fetch date
quoted_support: N/A -- absence noted directly: the full currency table (29 rows) lists Indonesian rupiah and Singapore Dollar as the only Southeast Asian currencies; Thai baht, Philippine peso, Vietnamese dong, and Malaysian ringgit do not appear.

claim: Upon closing an AdSense for YouTube account with a balance above the cancelation threshold, YouTube pays out the final balance within approximately 90 days after the end of the month, provided there are no holds and all pre-closure steps are completed.
stance_target: documented exit/payout timing for creators who stop monetizing
scope_conditions: global AdSense for YouTube accounts closed with balance above cancelation threshold
quoted_support: When you close your account, you'll get paid within approximately 90 days after the end of the month, as long as you: Don't have any holds; Have completed all of the steps to get paid before closing your account.

claim: The tax info threshold is set at USD 0 (or local-currency equivalent, often listed as N/A/immediate), meaning tax documentation is mandatory from the moment a creator enters YPP, before any revenue accrues.
quoted_support: If you're a creator in YPP, then you've hit the tax info threshold and need to submit your tax info, no matter your location.
